# Technical overview: visual review collaboration

Visual review is implemented as a read projection over Git-backed review records, with one guarded append path for discussion and spatial markup. The browser composes the authored visual, semantic Item controls, and projected feedback. The server binds a write to the content and source comparison the reviewer actually saw; the store serializes publication and retains earlier events. The five slides distill this design into an ownership diagram, a request sequence, a thread state model, a failure model, and an annotation model.

## Architecture and implementation strategy

The implementation separates three responsibilities: presenting the authored explanation, deriving the current review state, and recording a new action. `internal/server` adapts HTTP requests and renders the browser surfaces; `internal/reviewstate` derives reports and threads; `internal/reviewstore` validates and appends records through the Saga writer lock. `internal/saga` defines and loads the persisted model. This division keeps transport and presentation details outside the storage operation while making the same append boundary available to browser and CLI callers. The [ownership slide](annotation:ownership) is the visual summary of these boundaries.

| Boundary | Responsibility | State it owns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser review surface | Display slides and evidence controls; retain drafts; submit actions and apply confirmed feedback. | Transient DOM, draft, pending-save and uncertain-save state. |
| HTTP adapter | Bound and parse input, check the process token, resolve the review range, and supply the shown-snapshot check. | Request context and the server process's mutation token. |
| Read projection | Resolve the comparison, derive slide reports, group comment threads, and expose the current feedback. | Derived data; it does not publish review events. |
| Locked writer | Reload valid Saga state, resolve the canonical target, run mutation guards, and create an attributed event. | The publication boundary for durable records. |
| Git-backed records | Preserve review identity, authored decks, comments, annotation actions, and decisions. | Files that can be inspected and versioned with the repository. |

The [read projection](annotation:projection) and [locked writer](annotation:writer) operate on the same records but have different jobs. A page render is not a mutation. A successful store append is a durable action even if the subsequent feedback render fails. This distinction is reflected in the save response rather than hiding both operations behind a single success/failure flag.

![Visual ownership: browser surface, HTTP adapter, read projection, locked writer, and Git-backed records](slide:review-ownership)

## Persisted model and identity

The [storage model](annotation:records) uses stable review-scoped slide and Item targets. A comment names a target, so it stays attached to the semantic object instead of a transient DOM position. A reply joins an existing comment's canonical target; a supplied target does not redirect that reply to another object. Record identity and ordering are separate: an event has an ID and creation time, and the loader orders events by creation time with the ID as a deterministic tie-breaker.

| Record or field group | Meaning in the implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Review manifest and deck | Identify the review, its source comparison and authored slides; a recorded merged range makes the review historical. |
| `ReviewComment.id`, `target`, `reply_to` | Identify the event, its stable slide or Item, and its parent discussion event. A root has no `reply_to`. |
| `body`, `state` | Carry the comment text and optional explicit `open` or `resolved` thread state. A normal reply need not change state. |
| `reviewer`, `commit`, `created_at` | Preserve the declared reviewer identity, source commit when recorded, and event order. |
| `anchor`, `annotation_action` | Extend the same comment model with spatial markup and `create`, `update`, or `delete` actions. |
| Per-slide decision | Remains a separate record class from discussion. Thread resolution does not constitute approval. |

`ReviewAnchor` carries shapes or a text note in normalized visual coordinates. The [annotation model](annotation:markup) stores geometry outside the authored SVG or HTML, allowing feedback to move or disappear in the projected view while preserving the source visual and original discussion. Prototype annotations are a separate requirement-linking mechanism; they are not these review events.

## Read path: derive feedback without replacing the visual

The initial review page loads the Saga and review report, builds one slide view for each authored slide, and associates slide and Item threads with their stable targets. The visual is served separately. Item controls retain the routes to exact code evidence and linked living records; opening evidence is not a write. The [browser surface](annotation:ownership) and [comment sequence](annotation:round-trip) show how these pieces remain connected.

After a mutation, `reviewFeedbackFor` rebuilds only the selected slide's feedback: its decision/menu fragment, slide report, snapshot, frozen flag, and thread HTML keyed by slide or Item target. It requests a report with coverage calculation skipped. It does not rebuild file patches, coverage markup, the page shell, or the visual iframe. The [feedback projection](annotation:feedback) therefore limits the refresh to collaboration state.

In the browser, feedback application updates decision and range displays, thumbnail status, and existing thread containers. Newly received comments are inserted by event identity; existing reply forms are retained rather than replacing the entire slide. If the returned snapshot differs from the one originally shown, or the review has become frozen, write controls are disabled and the reader is told to reload. Receiving newer feedback does not silently replace the snapshot that authorized the old view.

## Write path: validate, lock, recheck, append

The browser sends URL-encoded fields with `Accept: application/json`, the process mutation token, and the immutable snapshot associated with the displayed slide. Comment fields include the target or reply ID, body, optional thread state, and optional annotation payload. A page-level pending flag prevents overlapping submissions from that page; it is not the cross-process concurrency mechanism. The [submission Item](annotation:round-trip) owns the client-side part of this sequence.

1. **HTTP preflight.** The adapter caps the request at 256 KiB and parses the form. It checks the mutation token, loads a valid Saga, finds the review, refuses a recorded merged review, and resolves its current source head. Malformed input is rejected before calling the writer. See the [input and authority gates](annotation:input-gate).
2. **Domain validation.** `reviewstore.Comment` checks body length, explicit state, reviewer identity, commit shape, and annotation action/anchor combinations. A normal comment requires text; an annotation action may receive a generated action description. The maximum body length is 20,000 Unicode code points. See [comment validation](annotation:validation).
3. **Lock and reload.** `mutate` acquires the shared Saga writer lock and reloads structurally valid records. The operation looks up the review again and rejects a recorded merged review. A reply resolves through an existing comment in that review; a root target resolves to an existing slide or Item. See the [durable critical section](annotation:critical-section).
4. **Recheck the shown view.** The HTTP-supplied callback resolves the range again and compares the fresh target's snapshot with the browser's submitted snapshot. A changed head, changed content/evidence, different checkout, or missing asynchronous snapshot rejects the write. See the [snapshot gate](annotation:snapshot).
5. **Publish one event.** Only after these checks does the store generate an event ID and write its new JSON record using exclusive creation. It returns the stored event and canonical target. This publication does not itself create a Git commit. See the [append operation](annotation:append).
6. **Return a receipt, then project.** The response identifies the saved event. Feedback is included when it can be rebuilt; projection failure becomes a warning attached to a successful save receipt. See [feedback projection](annotation:feedback).

![Comment write sequence: displayed slide, submitted snapshot, guarded append, and confirmed feedback](slide:comment-round-trip)

### What the snapshot protects

The snapshot binds the slide identity and digest to the resolved review range, then scopes that identity to the canonical source-checkout and Saga paths. The slide digest includes the manifest, visual, Items, and exact references. Feedback events deliberately do not enter this identity: another comment must not make the visual content the reviewer saw appear stale. The [snapshot gate](annotation:snapshot) is invoked inside the writer's critical section, after fresh records and the canonical target are available.

The lock serializes Saga mutations; it does not lock a Git branch against future pushes. A head movement after the check does not retarget the saved action: the event records the explicitly checked commit. Another important compatibility boundary remains: older ordinary forms without a snapshot may use the existing contract, whereas asynchronous requests require the snapshot. The implementation therefore does not promise identical optimistic-concurrency protection for every legacy caller.

## Thread and annotation projection

`reviewstate.Threads` first identifies root comments and reply-parent links, then follows each reply back to its root. A new root defaults to `open` unless it specifies a state. Replies are appended in the loader's event order; only a nonempty state changes the thread's projected state. Consequently, an ordinary reply after resolution leaves the thread resolved, while a later explicit `open` reopens it. Earlier events are not rewritten. The [reply-root resolution](annotation:reply-root) and [last-state transition](annotation:thread-state) are separate parts of this projection.

![Thread state model: a root, nested replies, explicit state transitions, and the append-only ledger](slide:thread-lifecycle)

Spatial markup is another projection over those threads. The annotations endpoint selects roots with `annotation_action=create` and an anchor, then folds their ordered actions into a current anchor and deleted flag. This read is separate from serving the authored slide, allowing the visual to be displayed before collaboration markup is loaded. See the [markup projection](annotation:markup).

| Annotation action | Required shape of the event | Projection effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create` | A new root with an anchor, no `reply_to`. | Establish the mark and its discussion thread. |
| `update` | An anchor and a reply directly to the annotation's creation root. | Replace the projected anchor and clear the deleted flag. |
| `delete` | A reply directly to that creation root, without an anchor. | Mark the projected annotation deleted; retain its events. |
| Ordinary reply | Text replying within the thread, without an annotation action. | Add discussion without changing the current geometry. |

Requiring updates and deletes to name the creation root prevents an otherwise valid-looking reply to a normal comment from becoming an unrenderable annotation mutation. The [domain validator](annotation:validation) enforces that ownership rule before publication. An update after a delete can project the mark as visible again; delete is an event, not physical erasure of the history.

## Failure semantics and recovery

A failed HTTP interaction does not always mean the store did not append. The [save-outcome model](annotation:save-outcomes) preserves that uncertainty explicitly instead of automatically replaying an action that may already exist.

| Observation | What the client can conclude | Resulting behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A pre-publication refusal, such as invalid input/token or changed snapshot | The request was refused. | Retain the draft. Allow correction when the current view remains writable; stale or frozen views require reload or stay read-only. |
| JSON receipt with `saved=true` and `event_id` | The event was appended. | Clear the submitted form and apply feedback. A feedback warning does not turn the saved action into a failed save. |
| Confirmed save, but feedback projection or application fails | Persistence succeeded; its display is incomplete. | Show a saved-with-warning message and offer a read-only feedback refresh. |
| Network error, server error, unreadable response, or missing receipt | Publication may or may not have happened. | Retain the draft, enter uncertain state, and block further writes from that page. |
| Read-only feedback fetch while uncertain | A current projection was observed; an earlier request may still finish. | Show the feedback, keep uncertainty, and require inspection/reload before resubmission. |

The browser's feedback check captures a local revision counter and discards the result if another submission has intervened or is pending. This prevents an older read response from overwriting newer feedback. It does not provide retry deduplication. The protocol should therefore be understood as guarded append plus explicit confirmation, not an exactly-once delivery guarantee across arbitrary retries.

## Invariants and design tradeoffs

- **One authoritative history.** Comments and annotation edits share attributed, append-only records. Resolving a thread or deleting a drawn mark changes the projection, not the preceding events. The [event ledger](annotation:ledger) makes these transitions inspectable.
- **One publication boundary.** The writer locks, reloads, resolves, and rechecks before creating a record. A handler's earlier successful lookup is insufficient authorization for a later append. The [critical section](annotation:critical-section) carries that guarantee.
- **Stable context.** A reply inherits its canonical target; a displayed snapshot binds the action to the shown slide and source range. Exact code remains attached to the existing Items rather than being duplicated in this document. See [snapshot validation](annotation:snapshot).
- **Cheap feedback refresh, retained visual context.** Feedback refresh excludes coverage and visual reconstruction. The cost is multiple derived surfaces to keep consistent: thread HTML, decision summaries, and the separate annotation projection. See [incremental feedback](annotation:feedback).
- **Recoverable ambiguity rather than blind replay.** A lost receipt sacrifices immediate resubmission to avoid silently duplicating an action. This is a deliberate behavior of the client protocol, with inspection/reload as its recovery boundary. See [uncertain outcomes](annotation:save-outcomes).

The design favors inspectable repository files and deterministic reconstruction over a separate mutable discussion database. As history grows, loading and projecting those records still has a cost; this overview makes no performance claim or exactly-once guarantee. The five slides summarize the mechanisms above, and their existing Items remain the route to the code and linked Product stories. Citing every slide connects the technical account to its visual digest; it does not independently establish code coverage or implementation correctness.

title: Visual review collaboration architecture
objective: Explain how slide-based discussion, spatial markup, and guarded append-only saves keep review feedback connected to its context.
